answer: A bonded identity protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock cryptographic titles to physical commodities, such as certified timber tracts or vaulted opal deposits, before voting at the consensus summit. An attacker must therefore expend substantial real-world capital to acquire scarce physical assets for every spawned entity. However, this design depends heavily on off-chain appraisal oracles, leaving the network vulnerable to fraudulent asset attestations.
